description: Helps you decide which leads are worth a seller's time. You give the criteria that matter, how important each one is and, if you know it, what goes with success. You get a lead scoring template: example point weights set by importance level, example points for each value you list, a scorecard and tier bands to adjust, with sector notes when your inputs name a supported sector. Your success pattern is matched to your criteria; it does not set the weights. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Without scoring_criteria, it returns a labelled example model. Invalid values return a correction error. Incomplete or failed held_back_test evidence holds the scoring decision. Use this instead of account_prioritization when you need a reusable scoring template before ranking named accounts. Ask for held-back test counts and the pre-agreed stop rule when a model has been tested.

company.description: Optional: your company or product name, so the answer can name it. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

correlation_direction.description: Optional confirmed direction of the success pattern. Ask the user whether the named values correlate with better or worse outcomes before filling this. Overrides word reading; unknown withholds a top-points recommendation. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "positive".

held_back_test.description: Optional results on deals held back before tuning. Ask for the counts and the stop rule set before the test. A missed rule holds the scoring model; do not tune on this set. Format is a JSON object. For example, {"wins_tested":20,"wins_passing":17,"non_wins_tested":20,"non_wins_passing":3,"minimum_win_pass_percent":80,"maximum_non_win_pass_percent":20}.

maximum_non_win_pass_percent.description: Format is a JSON number. For example, 20.

minimum_win_pass_percent.description: Format is a JSON number. For example, 80.

non_wins_passing.description: Format is a whole number. For example, 3.

non_wins_tested.description: Format is a whole number. For example, 20.

wins_passing.description: Format is a whole number. For example, 17.

wins_tested.description: Format is a whole number. For example, 20.

product_category.description: Optional: what you sell, as a product category, so the scoring notes use your sector. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

scoring_criteria.description: Criteria for scoring with importance levels. Format is a JSON array. For example, [{"criterion":"company size","importance":"critical","values":["200 to 500 employees"]}].

items.description: Format is a JSON object. For example, {"criterion":"company size","importance":"critical","values":["200 to 500 employees"]}.

criterion.description: Format is text. For example, "company size".

importance.description: Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "critical".

values.description: Format is a JSON array. For example, ["200 to 500 employees"].

items.description: Format is text. For example, "200 to 500 employees".

success_correlation.description: What correlates with success? (e.g., "deals with VP Sales champion close 2x faster"). Format is text.
